initial_executor.limitations: Evidence includes tests for occupational respiratory allergy (e1) which may differ from general allergic rhinitis; some tests like rhinomanometry (e5) evaluate symptoms (nasal obstruction) rather than confirming allergic etiology directly; nasal provocation tests are noted as gold standard or for inconclusive cases (e3, e15, e19); intradermal tests are evaluated for accuracy but skin prick is preferred (e24, e29); specific IgE in serum is an alternative for those susceptible to ID tests (e28).
